summary: East Dennis lookout in Benewah County: crow's nest 1915, two-tree platform 1932, 30-ft L-4 tower 1935, destroyed 1962; a 2022 post reports cement footings.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 30-ft pole tower
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed in 1962. An Idaho Fire Lookouts post (2022) says cement footings helped locate the site and that one footing was found nearby; nothing is left of the crow's nest and platform.

events.note: Crow's nest developed on the site, per firelookout.com; the 1915 Coeur d'Alene TPA report describes a lookout point established with a telephone link (Section 14)
Potlatch TPA annual report: the Forest Service improved 'Dennis Butte' (Section 15), which had not been used for lack of telephone service

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 feet, the height of the 1932 two-tree platform (Rex's page: 'Platform in two trees at the 20-foot level'). The 1935 pole tower that stood until 1962 is listed as 30 feet, about 9.1 m. The sources give pole height, not cab-floor height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1915 report places its lookout point in Section 14, and the 1921 report places Dennis Butte in Section 15. Rex's page lists both under East Dennis. The story does not say they are the same spot.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 6.1 m is the 1932 platform, not the 1935 tower; corrected to 9.1 m (30 ft pole height). Cab-floor height is not given. The 1915 and 1921 reports may describe the same butte (Sections 14 and 15 are adjacent) but the sources do not say so. The 1950 staffing is a single entry. A geocaching listing for this site appeared in search but could not be fetched, so it is not cited. No new photos added.
